Forget everything you know about magic and magicians… now remember it all again.
When
This Is Not a Magic Show
premiered in Edinburgh (UK) 10 years ago, it changed the rules of the game. This is a trailblazing work of theatre-magic in which Vincent Gambini questions the show itself, and all our expectations along with it.
It is both a unique performance of astonishing sleight-of-hand magic and a theatrical exploration of magic’s invisible mechanics, its clichés, and what it tells us about live performance and make-believe.
Cards transform inexplicably before our eyes, silver coins appear out of nowhere, and our own perception of reality explodes into a thousand mirrors.
Through his conversational yet crafted approach, Gambini presents a show within a show. It’s about magic, theatre, but mostly about ourselves, and how easily we suspend our disbelief.
Vincent Gambini is an award-winning, critically acclaimed magician and theatre artist based in the UK. He combines magic with elements of theatre, performance art, and spoken word to create new forms of deceptive theatre.
Over the last 20 years, his performances have taken place in theatres, arts centers, and galleries across the UK, Europe, and the United States.
Recent magic-theatre projects include the film
The Disappearing of Vincent Gambini
(2021), the intimate one-to-one performance Close-up, which toured UK seaside cafés (2024), and his latest book,
Compromised by Magic
(2026).
Vincent Gambini is the pseudonym of Augusto Corrieri, who, alongside his magic career, is a theatre artist and published writer.
"There’s something deeply satisfying in the chill, philosophical style of Vincent Gambini."
★★★★★ — Exeunt Magazine

In
Deconstructing The Music LIVE: The Beatles’ Abbey Road
, Scott Freiman, host of the Public Television series
Deconstructing the Beatles
, celebrates the Beatles’ groundbreaking 1969 album. Scott will take you on a track-by-track journey through this Beatles masterpiece, explaining the inspiration for the songs and their evolution in the studio.
Abbey Road was the last time that the Beatles recorded together at EMI Studios — soon-to-be-christened Abbey Road Studios after the album’s release. Despite the bittersweet atmosphere that surrounded the recording sessions, The Beatles’ outstanding songs and performances together with George Martin’s orchestrations produced an album that continues to be regarded as one of the best albums ever created. The album is filled with classic Beatles songs, such as “Come Together,” “Something,” and “Here Comes the Sun.” Martin told the Beatles to think “symphonically,” and they responded by creating the remarkable side two song suite.
Using rare audio and video clips, as well as anecdotes about the creation of the songs,
Deconstructing Abbey Road
explores the groundbreaking production techniques that went into producing this landmark piece of music history. Join Scott Freiman for this two hour exploration of the creation of Abbey Road.

The mission of
Hubbard Street Dance Chicago
is to awaken the human spirit through contemporary dance, envisioning a dance landscape that is relevant and accessible to all.
For 49 years, Hubbard Street has been one of the most original forces in contemporary dance – bringing top choreographers and works to Chicago and beyond. Hubbard Street’s ever-evolving repertory, created by today’s leading choreographic voices, makes us a company that dancers aspire to join and performance venues all over the world are eager to present. At home in Chicago, Hubbard Street performs 20 times a year and delivers renowned education programs in 50 classrooms across 17 Chicagoland schools. Tamayura: Echoes of the Soul
YAMATO: The Drummers of Japan
is a globally touring troupe based in Asuka-mura Nara Prefecture, a place well known by Japanese people as the hometown of Japan. Since their 1993 inception, with more than 4,000 performances across 54 countries, the work of YAMATO has brought energy and joy to thousands around the world.
YAMATO’s productions incorporate over 40 Taiko drums of different characters, sizes, and sounds. Their expert musicians train their bodies to the absolute limit to beat these massive instruments. While the acoustic pressure far surpasses what one could imagine, the ensemble’s acclaimed performances range from explosive percussion to delicate musical moments that offer a palette of meticulously crafted sound.
As the audience is engulfed in the sound of the Taiko—intense, sometimes sad, at times comforting, and even comical—they become one with the performers. People from all backgrounds gather around the power of Taiko, interweaving their lives and feeling the strength of one another’s passion and heart. Together, they create an unforgettable moment in which they feel truly alive.

Rhiannon Giddens has made a singular, iconic career out of stretching her brand of folk music, with its miles-deep historical roots and contemporary sensibilities, into just about every field imaginable. A two-time GRAMMY Award and Pulitzer Prize-winning singer and instrumentalist, MacArthur “Genius” grant recipient, and composer of opera, ballet, and film, Giddens has centered her work around the mission of lifting up people whose contributions to American musical history have previously been overlooked or erased, and advocating for a more accurate understanding of the country’s musical origins through art.
As Pitchfork once said, “few artists are so fearless and so ravenous in their exploration”—a journey that has led to NPR naming her one of its 25 Most Influential Women Musicians of the 21st Century and to American Songwriter calling her “one of the most important musical minds currently walking the planet.”
